questions.question: Where is the Vivekanand Rock Memorial situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanyakumari**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vivekanand Rock Memorial** is located in **Kanyakumari**, the **southernmost tip of mainland India**.
 
• The memorial was built in **1970 **in honor of **Swami Vivekananda** who is said to have attained enlightenment on the rock.
 
• It consists of two main structures - the **Vivekananda Mandapam** and the **Shripada Mandapam**.
 
• The memorial is a popular tourist destination and a place of pilgrimage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekananda** was a key figure in the introduction of Indian philosophies of **Vedanta and Yoga** to the Western world.
 
• He is also credited with raising interfaith awareness, bringing Hinduism to the status of a major world religion during the late 19th century.
 
• The rock memorial is situated about** 500 meters east of the mainland of Vavathurai**.
 
• Visitors can reach the memorial by taking a ferry service from the mainland.

costumes and make-up

questions.question: According to the first Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 report of NITI Aayog, which state in India ranks first?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bihar** ranks first according to the first **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 **report of NITI Aayog.
 
• The MPI is a comprehensive measure that uses various indicators to assess poverty beyond income-based metrics.
 
• It includes dimensions such as health, education, and standard of living to provide a more holistic view of poverty.
 
• This ranking highlights Bihar's high levels of multidimensional poverty compared to other states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** was developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• NITI Aayog's MPI report is the first of its kind for India, aiming to provide a more nuanced understanding of poverty at the state and district levels.
 
• The report uses data from the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)** and includes indicators like nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, and access to basic infrastructure.
 
• Efforts are being made by both the central and state governments to address the multidimensional aspects of poverty in Bihar and other high-ranking states.

questions.question: What is the full form of UPSC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Public Service Commission**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The full form of UPSC is **Union Public Service Commission**.
 
• UPSC is India's premier central recruiting agency responsible for appointments to and examinations for All India services and group A & group B of Central services.
 
• Established under **Article 315** of the Constitution of India, the UPSC conducts various exams such as the Civil Services Examination, Engineering Services Examination, and Combined Medical Services Examination, among others.
 
• The commission is mandated to ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process for the services under its purview.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **UPSC** was established on **1st October 1926** as the **Public Service Commission** but was later reconstituted as the **Federal Public Service Commission** by the **Government of India Act 1935**.
 
• **It was renamed as the Union Public Service Commission after independence**.
 
• UPSC is **headquartered **at **Dholpur House, New Delhi**.
 
• The commission is responsible for conducting exams for the recruitment of officers into the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and other central services.
 
• The chairman and other members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The commission operates under the guidance of the** Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**.
 
• UPSC ensures a merit-based selection process, thereby maintaining the integrity and efficiency of the civil services in India.

questions.question: To which of the state does Sattriya classical dance belong?

• This dance form originated in the state of **Assam**.
 
• Sattriya dance was introduced by the Vaishnav saint and reformer **Sankaradeva** in the 15th century.
 
• The dance form is a representation of the mythological narratives and teachings of Vaishnavism.
 
• It was traditionally performed in **Sattras (monasteries) **as a part of religious rituals and to convey spiritual messages.
 
• Sattriya has been recognized as a classical dance by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The dance form is characterized by expressive hand gestures, rhythmic footwork, and intricate body movements.
 
• The traditional attire for Sattriya dance includes a costume made of silk, adorned with traditional Assamese jewelry.
 
• The musical accompaniment for Sattriya includes instruments like the khol (a type of drum), taals (cymbals), and flute.
 
• Today, Sattriya dance has moved beyond the Sattras and is performed on various cultural platforms across India and the world.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barter system**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barter system** is not a function of money.
 
• Money serves as a **store of value**, enabling individuals to save and defer consumption until a later date.
 
• It acts as a **unit of account**, providing a common measure of the value of goods and services.
 
• Money functions as a **medium of exchange**, facilitating transactions between buyers and sellers.
 
• The **barter system** involves the direct exchange of goods and services without the use of money, which is different from the functions of money.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **barter system** was prevalent before the invention of money.
 
• While the barter system can work in small economies, it is inefficient in larger economies due to the **double coincidence of wants** problem, where two parties each possess an item the other wants.
 
• Money helps to overcome the limitations of the barter system by providing a common medium of exchange.
 
• By serving as a store of value, unit of account, and medium of exchange, money simplifies and enhances economic transactions.
 
• Modern economies rely on money to facilitate trade, savings, and economic calculation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The** 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, added the fundamental duty of providing opportunities for education to children between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• This amendment also led to the insertion of **Article 21A **in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children in this age group.
 
• The amendment emphasizes the role of parents and guardians in ensuring that children receive the necessary education.
 
• This duty reflects the importance placed on education as a means of individual and societal development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** fundamental duties** are enshrined in** Part IV-A **of the Constitution of India, under Article 51A.
 
• Originally, ten fundamental duties were listed, but the 86th Amendment Act added an eleventh duty.
 
• The concept of fundamental duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union and was added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens to respect the ideals and institutions of the nation.
 
• While these duties are non-justiciable, they are considered essential for the overall development and unity of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following rocks are formed during rock metamorphism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slate**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Slate** is a type of **metamorphic rock** that is formed through the metamorphism of shale.
 
• Metamorphic rocks are formed under the influence of **high pressure and temperature**, which alter the mineral composition and structure of the original rock.
 
• Other examples of metamorphic rocks include **schist, gneiss, and marble**.
 
• Metamorphism can occur due to tectonic processes such as continental collisions, which generate significant pressure and heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conglomerate** and **Sandstone** are examples of **sedimentary rocks**, which are formed from the accumulation and lithification of sediment.
 
• **Basalt** is an example of an** igneous rock**, which is formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
 
• Metamorphic rocks often **exhibit foliation, a layered or banded appearance** resulting from the alignment of mineral grains under directional pressure.
 
• Metamorphism can be regional, affecting large areas of the crust, or contact, occurring adjacent to igneous intrusions where heat is a dominant factor.
